freshness_notes.thames_water_dwmp28: statutory planning cycle under development; draft consultation planned November 2027
freshness_notes.caa_new_icao_ols: future applicability 21 November 2030; not current rule

batches.t: UK Power Networks licence-area / operator gate
batches.c: UK Power Networks owns and maintains electricity distribution networks across London, the East and South East. Exact candidate service/licence area and connection point must be confirmed before treating operator data as site evidence.
LTDS provides five-year network load forecasts, assets and planned developments. Published headroom is planning evidence, not a guaranteed connection offer or firm site capacity.

NDP and Network Scenario Headroom outputs look beyond current conditions under DFES scenarios. Scenario headroom must not be promoted as present firm capacity without a site-specific connection study.

SVI shows approximate network and substation locations and existing connections. Approximate geospatial infrastructure must not be treated as surveyed cable/substation position or legal easement evidence.

batches.t: Distribution Future Energy Scenarios demand-growth gate
batches.c: DFES models alternative pathways for EVs, heat pumps, generation and demand to 2050. Scenario forecasts are strategic planning evidence and not a parcel-specific load entitlement.

batches.t: Grid Supply Point capacity-visibility / queue gate
batches.c: GSP capacity and queue tools improve visibility of spare capacity and projects ahead. They do not replace a formal connection application, network study or accepted quotation.
Connections Lab and curtailment data support flexible-connection scenario analysis. Estimated curtailment is modelled and queue-dependent; it is not guaranteed operational performance.

Flexible connections can accelerate connection by accepting export constraints. Candidate viability requires an actual offer, constraint set and curtailment report; generic availability is not parcel capacity.
Connection products vary by required capacity and timing. Product availability does not establish that requested demand can be served at a candidate without reinforcement or constraints.

Connections Reform reordered the national connection pipeline. Zonal and pipeline information is system-level and cannot be translated into a distribution-site connection date or capacity without exact network studies.

In-scope connection contracts can include milestones for statutory consents, land rights and network interfaces. A planning candidate should not be treated as grid-secured until the relevant accepted offer and milestones are evidenced.

Regional development and reinforcement programmes may unlock future capacity, sometimes ahead of reinforcement. Proposed or planned reinforcement is not operational capacity until delivery and connection conditions are verified.
Developer enquiries first require confirmation that the site is in the operator service area. No candidate is assigned water or wastewater capacity from borough location alone.

Thames Water offers site-specific pre-planning capacity enquiries and can identify required upgrades. Only a returned site-specific capacity response can support a candidate; general network coverage is insufficient.
New mains and service connections depend on exact point of connection, design, permissions and programme. General presence of a nearby main is not proof of available capacity.
Where a supply area is water stressed, efficiency incentives and demand management can affect development assumptions. Provider-area status and scheme-specific demand must be verified before use.
A sewer connection requires the correct sewer type, point of connection and capacity assessment. A mapped sewer or manhole alone does not establish hydraulic capacity for the proposed discharge.

Thames Water requires build-over controls for works close to public sewers or laterals. Exact surveyed sewer ownership, diameter and distance are required before treating this as a candidate constraint.
Where connection requires third-party land or strategic/trunk sewer works, requisition or other delivery routes may be needed. Land-access and route evidence must be exact and project-specific.
Surface-water discharge to foul or combined sewer is not a default solution. The drainage hierarchy, attenuation, discharge point and operator approval must be resolved for the actual proposal.
Treatment works, pumping stations and storm tanks can create odour encroachment risk. Exact asset proximity and operator risk assessment are required before any candidate impact is promoted.
DWMP28 considers population change, climate change, asset health and future regulation. It is strategic system planning, not evidence that a specific site currently has or lacks wastewater capacity.

Work on or near operational railway infrastructure can require Asset Protection involvement. Exact railway asset proximity and proposed works must be established; borough-level rail presence is not a parcel constraint.
ASPRO covers work within designated precautionary areas of level crossings. Exact crossing, precautionary area and development traffic/access effects are required before promotion.
Construction equipment, excavation, piling, scaffolding and cranes can create rail safety risks. Assessment depends on exact geometry, method and railway assets, not a generic distance assumption.

Utilities crossing Network Rail land can require property rights such as easements plus Asset Protection agreements. Both legal and engineering approvals are project-specific and must not be inferred from route proximity.

Network Rail identifies many categories of third-party project risk and uses formal agreements/assurance. A candidate needs the applicable risk/asset assessment; strategic rail adjacency alone is insufficient.
Rail enhancement or capacity projects may support future growth but planned works are not an existing transport-capacity benefit until funding, delivery and operational status are verified.

Officially safeguarded aerodromes lodge maps with LPAs and can be statutory consultees. Exact site location, map cell and development parameters are required; a broad radius is not a parcel constraint.
OLS protects airspace around aerodromes. Exact coordinates, ground level, proposed building/equipment height and applicable aerodrome surface are required before determining infringement.

batches.t: Crane / tall construction equipment notification gate
batches.c: Crane and tall-equipment rules depend on height and aerodrome proximity, with additional en-route requirements. Construction-stage equipment must be assessed separately from completed-building height.

batches.t: CNS / radar / Instrument Flight Procedure safeguarding gate
batches.c: Development can affect communications, navigation, surveillance and IFPs even without direct OLS infringement. Exact technical safeguarding assessment by the relevant operator/APDO is required.
Aerodrome safeguarding can address wildlife attraction, lighting, reflective materials and plumes. These are proposal-design effects and cannot be assigned from a parcel coordinate alone.

CAA is preparing for new ICAO OLS applicability from 21 November 2030. Future surfaces may expand or reduce protected volumes, but must not be applied as current rules before their effective transition.
